explanations: Only one species, the Galapagos penguin, lives at the equator and slightly north of it.
A spiny tongue and powerful jaws grip slippery prey, which is swallowed whole while swimming.
The largest living species is the emperor, about 1.1 metres tall and 35 kilograms on average.
Some prehistoric species were enormous, as tall or as heavy as an adult human.
They are flightless, semi-aquatic sea birds with flippers for swimming, living almost entirely in the Southern Hemisphere.

sources.excerpt: Only one species, the Galapagos penguin, lives at, and slightly north of, the equator.
A penguin has a spiny tongue and powerful jaws to grip slippery prey.
Most penguins feed on krill, fish, squid and other forms of sea life which they catch with their bills and swallow whole while swimming.
The largest living species is the emperor penguin (Aptenodytes forsteri): on average, adults are about 1.1 m (3 ft 7 in) tall and weigh 35 kg (77 lb).
Some prehistoric penguin species were enormous: as tall or heavy as an adult human.
Penguins are a group of flightless semi-aquatic sea birds which live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: auks and puffins are northern birds and can fly; the great auk was flightless but of the north Atlantic, not the Southern Hemisphere; seals swim with flippers but are not birds.
